summary: Project updates store the revision of the default branch only; a job using a non-default branch pulls the newest revision right before it starts (so offline runs are impossible), and tags or commit hashes give a static version. The Source control branch and Playbook fields are not validated up front.
questions: Why does a job with a non-default branch need access to the git remote?
How do I pin a job to a fixed version of my project?
Does a project update save all branches?
Why isn't my playbook validated when branch override is used?

answer_card.title: Branch override and project revisions
answer_card.answer_md:
- A project update stores the revision of the **default** branch only.
- If a job uses a non-default *Source control branch* (not a tag or commit hash), controller pulls the newest revision from the remote just before the job starts, so these jobs cannot run offline.
- To run a fixed version, use a **tag or commit hash**.
- The *Source control branch* field is not validated, and when it is set or prompted the template's *Playbook* is not validated either; launch the template to check the playbook exists.
